MAJOR: `authorityReasonCode` now classifies any error whose lowercased message contains `"tls"` or `"password authentication"` as `db_unavailable`; substring `"tls"` also matches unrelated words (e.g. "defaults", "results") — over-broad classification risks mislabeling genuine internal errors as availability failures and skewing the bounded reason diagnostics.
MINOR: `backlogReserve` changed to `s.reserveBacklog()` which calls `s.backlogFactory("", true)`; the empty tenant is now hard-coded inside the new helper rather than at the call site, removing the documented "admin-only, no tenant binding" context from the seam — a future factory caller may assume tenant scoping, so add a doc comment on `reserveBacklog` making the deliberate unbound store explicit.

`authorityBacklog`/`reserveBacklog` duplicate the `edpdata.NewBacklog(...).WithTimeout(s.cfg.DBTimeout)` construction; the timeout wiring is now expressed twice, so a future change to the default timeout/backlog constructor must be kept in sync in both helpers.

New test `TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` mutates `s.backlogFactory` after the initial failure assertion and asserts recovery — good, but no test asserts that `reserveBacklog`'s unbound factory path (`tenant=""`) is exercised, leaving the reserve seam untested for the tenant-binding invariant.
NIT: The `57014`/`statement timeout` fallback is checked before `errors.As(err, &netErr)`; ordering is fine today but unreachable for `*pgconn.PgError` users — consider a dedicated `errors.As(&pgErr)` branch for clarity and to avoid string matching on `"57014"`.

`TestAuthorityFailureMetricUsesBoundedReasons` uses `strings.Contains(..., "edp_backlog_authority_errors_total{reason=\"internal_error\"}")` without the value; the earlier exact-value assertion was relaxed, weakening the metric-shape check.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves prior MAJORs (timeout precedence, request-only gauge, recovery assertion, textual markers) and cleanly splits `backlogFor` into `authorityBacklog`/`reserveBacklog`.
Main residual risk is the over-broad `"tls"` substring marker in `authorityReasonCode`, which can misclassify non-availability errors and pollute diagnostics; tighten the marker set.
Minor reuse/duplication between the two backlog helpers and an untested reserve seam are worth addressing but not blocking.
